title: Zabaglione (wine-free)
summary: Egg yolks whisked over simmering water into a warm, airy foam, spooned over a few berries; this version swaps the Marsala for rum extract and lemon.
steps: Divide the berries among four glasses.
Bring a few centimetres of water to a bare simmer in a saucepan. In a heatproof bowl that sits above, not in, the water, whisk the yolks and powdered erythritol until pale.

Add the water, lemon juice, rum extract and vanilla. Set the bowl over the pan and whisk constantly for 6–8 minutes, until the mixture triples in volume and holds a ribbon; it should reach about 70 °C (160 °F).
Spoon the warm foam over the berries and serve at once.
tips: If the bowl gets too hot the yolks scramble at the edges; lift it off the heat for a few seconds while you keep whisking.
A splash of strong brewed coffee in place of half the water makes a good variation.

origin.history: Zabaglione is a foam of egg yolks, sugar and sweet wine, usually Marsala, whisked over heat. Several Italian cities claim it, and the best-known stories, which credit Turin or a Renaissance court, are legends rather than documented history. It is related to the French sabayon, which is the same technique.
